items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: "all the musicians, they would come to our friend Don Payne’s house." and "And our friend Don Payne wrote it too."

ctx.x: The front gate is of a huge dog, this high, one on each side, and you walk through them and that’s the entrance to the grounds. There was a 350-year-old copper beech tree on the grounds, and up the hill was the Dodge estate, and that became, in the winter, a sledding hill, and it was a dangerous hill, because our drummer, who had been a paratrooper, he and I went sledding. And we’d go down this hill and you’d make a turn here go up around this one and go along this path, and he went over the path and he fell down…

It was like heaven though, you know, because it was great for the kids, it was a great neighborhood for them to be in, and we just really enjoyed it for eleven years. Oh and all the Brazilians came there too because every time, at that time, when anybody was coming to New York from Brazil, all the musicians, they would come to our friend Don Payne’s house.
Because he had been in Brazil with Tony Bennett.
